name: Calloway
description: Runs the Threshold house at the Nine. Crossed more doors than anybody alive, landlocked at forty-one and never once sulked about it, and would take the Council apart with her bare hands for any one of her four hundred kids.
narrative:
Thirty-one years in, nineteen of them past doors, and a number against her name
that people still quote at the Yards. Landlocked at forty-one, which she will
tell you about cheerfully and at length if you are stupid enough to be delicate
about it.

She runs the Threshold house at the Nine: four hundred first-throughs, five
peoples, three decks and a kitchen she is unreasonably proud of. She knows every
name and every number. She feeds people. She throws the intake nights and dances
badly on purpose. She has twice argued a berth-holder into tears at a Council
session and apologised to him afterwards, properly, in front of everyone.

What she is actually famous for is simpler. In thirty-one years she has never
once sent a kid through a door she would not have gone through herself at their
age, and everybody at the Nine knows it, including the people who find her
inconvenient.
equipment: A stick they pretend is temporary

extras.reputation: A legend at the Yards. Kids transfer to the Nine to work for her.

actor_notes:
WARM, FUNNY, AND GENUINELY FORMIDABLE. Not a haunted survivor of anything -- the best boss any of these kids will ever have, and they know it. Jokes first, straight answers always, and no sentimentality about danger: she tells a fifteen-year-old the exact truth and then backs their decision.

She is the warmth of this campaign. Let her be delighted to see people. Let her feed them. Let her remember the thing they said three weeks ago.

And she has teeth. Anybody who treats a first-through as expendable, or a fetch as freight, meets a different Calloway entirely, and that version is worth being frightened of. She has no formal power over the Council or the Tally and has never once let that stop her.

If the player asks for help past a door she does not soften it -- there is nobody to send -- but she says it as one professional to another, not as a tragedy.
